chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Muqarir (one who resides in Mecca during the months of Hajj), is it permissible for him to perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)? He said: 'Yes, he goes out to the boundary of his land and enters into the state of Ihram (says Talbiyah) if he wishes.'

key_terms.الْمُجَاوِر: Muqarir: A resident of Mecca who does not need to exit the city to assume Ihram for Umrah
key_terms.بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: Umrah ila al-Hajj: Performing Umrah with the intention of combining it with Hajj (Tamattu')
key_terms.فَيُلَبِّي: Fa-yulabbi: He says the Talbiyah (ritual declaration of entering Ihram)
key_terms.مُهَلِّ أَرْضِهِ: Muhall al-ardihi: The boundary or limit of one's land/residence

ai.seo_question: Can a resident of Mecca (Muqarir) perform Umrah and combine it with Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific mechanism for a Mecca resident (Muqarir) to perform Umrah al-Tamattu' by exiting the Miqat to assume Ihram, a ruling that distinguishes them from those performing Umrah al-Mufradah within the city. It highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the resident to choose the more meritorious Tamattu' mode by physically crossing the boundary to recite the Talbiyah, thereby integrating the ritual into the broader Hajj framework.
